speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Ms Rahayu Mahzam spoke about this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has not abated; it has probably intensified.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, to guard against social fault lines, and segregationist tendencies are of the biggest concern.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Minister has already explained how we go about it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, to make it harder for the terrorists to carry out attacks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Make them think twice, thrice if possible, before they target us.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When it happens, we will be shocked, but we must not be immobilised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will expand on the latter two strategies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have made significant moves to enhance preparedness and deter attacks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Last year, we amended the Public Order Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are coming to Parliament to seek Members' support because the Police may need the additional powers to protect public safety for serious incidents like a terror attack.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This does not mean that the Police is not, at the same time, doing other things, such as enhancing operational response capabilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are officers who patrol the areas of high human traffic, for example, Orchard Road and Marina Bay.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We started them because it was the festive season.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If something happens, they can intervene more swiftly and effectively until the other forces arrive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Mr Desmond Choo rightly pointed out that the preparedness must go beyond the Home Team.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Every Singaporean has a role to play, and that is why community partnership is a key part of the Home Team's work, and also why we launched the SGSecure movement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are now moving into the next phase of SGSecure.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What that means is that from awareness, we now focus on preparedness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One focal point is workplaces because everyone goes to work every single day.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are very much a part of our lives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are advisories that the employers can distribute to their staff.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And what it does is to guide people on what they can do in an attack – where to hide safely, how to perform improvised first-aid because you will not have all the essential materials that usually are associated with first-aid, you have to improvise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Overall, we are making good progress in enhancing deterrence and preparedness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we cannot let our guard down and we must continue to press on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo has asked for a progress update.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Home Team Transformation has to be a multi-year effort but with a clear and consistent purpose and, that is, to renew and strengthen our capabilities, so that we can remain a prepared, effective and trusted force.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Technology is a big part of that transformation journey.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One, to counter emerging threats and, two, to improve our effectiveness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Terrorist groups are seeking to develop such capabilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What they plan to do is to use viruses or infectious diseases as weapons.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: How do we know that this is happening?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Al-Qaeda has an encyclopedia of Jihad, and in the 11th volume of this encyclopedia of Jihad, it is entirely devoted to chemical and biological weapons.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And, of course, when terrorists are captured, the reports also show that they admit to such plots.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question is why are biological weapons attractive to terrorists?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The reasons are because they are hard to detect, it is not immediately observable that a biological attack has taken place and, by the time it is known, there will already be many victims.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It can cause widespread panic and the public could be gripped by fear.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They could either self-quarantine themselves or they want to avoid contact.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That poses a major risk for a place like Singapore where many people pass through our borders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are a global and regional hub for business, finance, aviation and maritime matters.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo will be happy to know that this Lab-on-Chip system that is in use at our borders is developed by a local company Veredus Laboratories.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, it can test for multiple biological threats, not just one.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Compared to traditional screening methods, you need four times as long, 12 hours.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has also been tested elsewhere in Singapore, at large-scale public events, and when epidemic outbreaks elsewhere are at risk of reaching our shores.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But thankfully, no incident of bio-terrorism agents has been detected so far.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we have developed the capability and, in case it happens, we can take preventive or mitigation measures more quickly, so as to reduce the spread of viruses and diseases.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Technology is also being used to improve our operational effectiveness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is cutting down time spent on routine tasks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is helping our officers to do more with less, and it is helping to reduce the exposure of our officers to dangerous situations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What this UFM does is that it can shoot giant jets of water to extinguish fires, and it is remotely controlled.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, it can go deep into dangerous areas and it is much less risky than deploying our officers to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has proven its usefulness in fighting major fires at Sungei Kadut, Jurong Island and Tuas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It can help SCDF officers lift heavier loads, so that they can sustain operations for a longer period of time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another game-changer in Home Team Transformation is something we are all, as Members of Parliament, quite familiar with, and that is the Police Camera (PolCam) initiative.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police have been coming down very hard on unlicensed moneylenders and they have successfully curtailed all of these cases that I have mentioned, especially those that involved physical harassment or confrontation because they caused damage to property.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police have been relentless and, as a result, the unlicensed moneylending syndicates have been forced to change their modus operandi and find other methods of harassment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh spoke about the spike in moneylending harassment in 2013.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These were mostly cases that did not involve damage to property.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They involved non-physical forms of harassment, such as through text messages and social media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are not necessarily a sign of heightened loan shark activity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It could simply be due to the proliferation of online messaging services, and also the easily available technological tools to mask the identities of the senders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But naturally, the victims are distressed and the harassment by text messages and online means are much harder to prevent and to crack.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We deal with them in a few ways.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, people should know that unlicensed moneylending is illegal and, if they borrow from unlicensed moneylenders, they risk becoming the victims of harassment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, if the borrowers are harassed by unlicensed moneylenders, they get protection from the Harassment Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This provides a means for victims to seek protection.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If harassment involves threats, hurt and property damage, the victims should report the cases to the Police and the Police will investigate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If it is found to have been grievous, they will take action against the perpetrators.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the resources we have are limited and the public should also play its part – do not borrow from unlicensed moneylenders in the first place and to advise family and friends against doing so, and also to seek help through other means.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are just some of the examples that the Home Team is using technology to counter emerging threats and enhance our effectiveness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a result of these efforts, technology investments will increase significantly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It demonstrates our resolve to remain effective, even with rising terror threats and manpower constraints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The value of technology lies in how it is used.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Job redesign will, therefore, be a big part of this effort.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will help to ensure that Home Team jobs remain relevant and challenging and will allow our officers to maximise their value-add.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One example is the ICA's Buss Scanning Project.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You can find it at the Tuas Checkpoint where two radiographic imaging scanners are being installed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What these two scanners do is to scan all the arriving buses to detect anomalies, such as hidden compartments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: How does it help the officers and the Home Team?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Well, their time and attention are freed up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can use the scanning results to perform targeted checks instead of performing checks on all the buses.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What this means is that it gives the real criminals a harder time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of course, the officers need training to reskill and reorientate and they are getting that retraining.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They learn X-ray image analysis and also how to do security profiling using analytics.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About 40 officers have been trained so far.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how retiring officers are being supported in job placement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To remind the House, the retirement age was raised from 50 to 55 in 2013.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Career Transition Office for Home Team officers was set up in 2016.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is helping retiring officers to find employment within the Home Team or public sector agencies as civilian officers, or with private sector companies, for example, security firms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It also recognises that, for the officers, adjustments are needed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the officers can try out potential job opportunities, whether at public agencies or private sector companies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo also suggested further ideas for transforming the Home Team.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are all good ideas and we will seriously consider them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about plans to transform the private security industry.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Security ITM was recently launched and it is a tripartite effort among the Government, security service providers as well as the buyers and the union.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Productivity gains for security service providers, cost savings or better value for service buyers, better employment outcomes for security personnel and a more secure Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng hopes that older workers can continue to contribute and I fully agree with him.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have seen how it can be done.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the security industry is not a profession that shuts out seniors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the contrary, even with the use of technology, we will see them playing an active role.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Technology can help to take over labour-intensive tasks, for example, ground patrols, and it will make work easier for the older security officers who can still have a meaningful role, tap their experience, make judgements when security alerts through video analytics, for example, are presented to them and advise their younger colleagues on the best response.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Government support is available for job redesign and WDA offers customised guidance and funding support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng highlighted his concern that security training materials are not written in simple English.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The training standards are set by SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) in consultation with the Police and other industry stakeholders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, they can use videos for instruction and, instead of written tests, they can take oral assessments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Experienced security officers also do not have to attend classroom training or take written tests.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can obtain a Statement of Attainment through an assessment-only pathway, which means face-to-face interviews and role play.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Edwin Tong spoke about having sufficient qualified security consultants for purposes of the Infrastructure Protection Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He asked if there are other qualifications that can be considered, and the answer is yes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The tripartite partners have a joint stake in the Security ITM and we are confident we will achieve the vision of a security industry that is vibrant, technologically-advanced and competitive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, if you will allow me, I would like to conclude in Mandarin.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In Mandarin):   In the coming years, we will continue to review and enhance our laws, upgrade our procedures, and focus on the transformation of the Home Team.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will invest significantly in technology to counter emerging threats and improve the effectiveness of the Home Team.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As laptops and smartphones have become common, the number of criminal cases involving digital media has gone up manifold.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To investigate these crimes, information and evidence need to be extracted from digital devices, such as handphones and thumb drives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not sustainable to maintain the status quo in the way we approach the investigation and handling of evidence for such crimes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This kiosk will also be able to scan for possible evidence based on the type of case being investigated.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Overall, this will allow our IOs to quickly access evidence and carry out their investigations more effectively.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even as we invest in technologies and systems, we will also ensure that our officers are given the necessary training and retraining so that they can continue to contribute effectively in their roles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Beyond our transformation efforts, ultimately, it is the professionalism and dedication of each and every Home Team officer that matters the most.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They put in a lot of hard work to keep us safe and secure, even when the rest of Singapore is enjoying our public holidays or asleep at home, and, oftentimes, they go beyond their call of duty to serve our people.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The public’s trust and confidence in the Home Team continues to be high.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not take it for granted, however, and will strive to continue to deserve this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, I will focus on two areas: first, keeping Singapore drug-free; and second, supporting the rehabilitation and reintegration of offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza spoke about stemming the supply and demand of drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Keeping Singapore drug-free is a key priority for MHA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This requires a combination of tough laws, effective enforcement and preventive education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Just last week, CNB had a joint operation with their Malaysian counterparts to smash a regional drug syndicate.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Baey Yam Keng spoke about emerging drug threats, such as the purchase of drugs online and new psychoactive substances.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are people in Singapore who have tried to buy drugs online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They thought they could get away with it.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to clamp down on the online drug trade.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: New psychoactive substances (NPS) are a global challenge that many countries are grappling with.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: So far, the NPS situation in Singapore is contained.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is because we keep a close watch for any new substances, and list them in MDA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Regular reviews of our legislative and operational strategies are conducted to combat NPS abuse.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To keep Singapore drug-free, all Singaporeans must know that drugs are harmful and stay away from them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Edwin Tong and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked how we can better engage youths and tackle the high proportion of new and young drug abusers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In 2017, two out of five abusers arrested were new abusers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is very worrying and there are foreign celebrities who glamourise drug use and they falsely advocate drugs as harmless and "cool".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Minister earlier mentioned about the Portuguese campaign "Say no to second-hand syringes".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We advocate a life free from addiction and we encourage our youths to enjoy life to the fullest and make the best of life's opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Be drug-free – these are taglines that are trending here in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is the narrative: we reject drugs and we reject the notion that drugs are harmless or "cool".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They destroy life, health and family; and drug abuse is not a victimless crime.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have ramped up our preventive drug education efforts in the last year, both on the ground and on social media.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Besides school programmes and roadshows, CNB collaborated with education institutions and young local filmmakers to produce a series of videos showing the destructive effect of drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Eighteen short films were posted on CNB's Instagram and Facebook with the handle #FilmFriday, racking up close to two million views in total.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To reach out to more youths, CNB also set up a makeshift club called “GURD Club” outside Cathay Cineplex. “GURD Club” featured lights and sounds which simulated the disorientating and distressing effects of drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our community is with us in this fight against drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our United Against Drugs Coalition partners include Pastamania and Singapore Post, just to name a few, and they have helped to distribute 50,000 "DrugFreeSG" keychains to the public during our Anti-Drug Abuse Campaign last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Online retailer Reebonz distributed 5,000 anti-drug message cards in their parcels during Christmas last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam spoke about engaging the community, especially the Malay Muslim community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to speak in Malay on this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   The good news is that we received strong support from the Malay/Muslim community in various efforts to combat the drug menace.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Last April, six Malay/Muslim organisations led by the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) launched a campaign called Drugs are Forbidden in Islam.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This was an initiative by the community leaders in order to increase awareness about Islam’s prohibition on drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These include 50 barber shops that have a reach of 10,000 customers per week.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These "big brother barbers" and "barber uncles" are helping to spread the anti-drug message by displaying stickers stating "Drugs are Forbidden in Islam" at their shops’ entrances and mirrors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Last month, I had a haircut in Woodlands North Plaza.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The barber, in fact, asked for more stickers from the Drugs Are Forbidden in Islam campaign.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: He replied, many of his customers saw the sticker and asked if they can have the sticker for themselves.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: About 200 motorcycle enthusiasts also helped to mobilise their network to spread the message of “Drugs Are Forbidden in Islam” to places frequented by youths and hawker-centres around Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I joined their public outreach efforts from Bedok to Arab Street, then we stopped by Bukit Batok, then to Jurong and onwards to Woodlands and many other places to spread awareness about the drug menace.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is certainly a true community effort – an effort by youths for youths – a truly noble effort.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The riders include Mr Ramle Ismail and also Mr Azri Zulfarhan Kamsin, a 30-year-old Institute of Technical Education (ITE) lecturer.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They deployed the motorcycle group networks to reach out to youths every month, by going to youth hangouts and eating establishments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Apart from them, a group of Malay/Muslim undergraduates led by the Malay Language Society from the National University of Singapore (NUS) also chipped in to help out in anti-drug efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is our pledge: we will continue to strongly support the community’s efforts in the "Drugs Are Forbidden in Islam" campaign.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to work closely with Malay/Muslim organisations, like Jamiyah, Pertapis, the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP), Muhammadiyah, and the Singapore Muslim Women’s Association, in order to enhance efforts to free our community from prohibited drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are truly determined to ensure that our children, whom we love, are protected from the drug menace.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We dream of a community that is free from prohibited drugs that destroy our youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am confident that, when we keep working hand in hand, we will surely achieve this dream.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In English): Let me now turn to the second area of focus: supporting the rehabilitation and reintegration of offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked if MHA can consider quashing criminal records of drug offenders who stay free from drugs for three to four years to facilitate their reintegration into society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will consider how else we can support the reintegration of drug offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Louis Ng spoke about the importance of programmes in prison, and family and social support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: He asked if SPS will be extending family programmes to more inmates.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPS works with community partners, like Focus on the Family, The Salvation Army and Singapore Children's Society, to conduct bonding programmes for inmates and their families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have structured family programmes run by agencies, such as Fei Yue Community Services and Lakeside Family Services, to strengthen family relationships.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPS aims to extend family programmes to more inmates.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Another factor that can reduce re-offending is social support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPS has established a Befriending Programme for trained volunteers to befriend inmates and support them upon release.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if SPS would consider having more programmes featuring ex-offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We agree that sharing by ex-offenders can be very impactful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPS collaborates with community partners to engage ex-offenders to give monthly motivational talks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In addition to face-to-face talks, the talks are also uploaded on shared tablets which are being piloted for inmates to engage in self-learning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Employment is another key in breaking the offending cycle.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Edwin Tong asked for an update on plans to enhance the employability of ex-offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCORE provides skills training, job placement, job coaching and job retention support to help ex-offenders reintegrate into the workforce.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This year, SCORE will be launching several initiatives to enhance the employability of inmates.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In other words, inmates can have a job coach for a year after their release.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will equip inmates with vocational skills in demand by potential food and beverage (F&B) employers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And we will explore having WSQ Advanced Training in other sectors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, supporting offenders in their rehabilitation journey is not easy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For some, it takes more than one attempt.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are with them each step of the way.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I first met Lina after her release from prison in 2016.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: She had found a new job through SCORE and I thought she was coping well.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But months later, I met her again when I visited our Prison School for a National Youth Achievement Award Ceremony.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: She saw me and she said, "I am sorry, I have let you down." I said to her, “We have not given up on you.” And that, Mr Chairman, is also what our officers do.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But we also believe very strongly in rehabilitating and reintegrating inmates.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our Prison School has, at its entrance, a lighthouse mural.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This symbolises our efforts to shine light towards a bright path, a path that leads the way from the darkness of drugs, a path that guides those who have strayed, to a fulfilling life towards a brighter future.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Keeping Singapore safe and secure is a whole-of-Singapore effort.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: From our Home Team officers to our community partners, volunteers and citizens, each of us plays an important part in making Singapore our Safe and Secure Home.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Chairman, I have a clarification to ask of the Second Minister who spoke about Home Team transformation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have a manpower-lean environment and an ageing population which means that the SCDF emergency call numbers are going to continue to rise.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, I was wondering how will MHA and the Home Team work to address this, please.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will have to find ways to cope.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One, we will have to grow our fleet of emergency ambulances, but we also have to make better use of our limited resources.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The severe cases that are life-threatening, like you have a cardiac arrest or a loss of consciousness, those are of the highest priority.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because in a cardiac arrest – Dr Tan Wu Meng would know this – another minute of delay and you would have about 7% to 10% reduction in probability of survival.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we need to give it the highest priority.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But not every 995 call is a life-threatening emergency.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As incredible as it may sound, we have had people called us for constipation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If that translates to an average of two non-emergency calls every hour, and someone calls in and you have a cardiac arrest but the SCDF resources are tied up, then we will be in serious trouble.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we have to prioritise and the target time to respond to different types of calls will not be the same.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But unless we do so, no amount of resources will be enough to make sure that the critical cases are always attended to first.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I just want to clarify on the effectiveness of SGSecure.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Has SGSecure been effective in increasing awareness and also preparedness of Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: My second clarification is to the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It has to do with the drug issue, not a new issue.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am just wondering if the Ministry conducts studies and also perhaps use behavioural insights to inform it and to help it in its preventive drug outreach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, the National Security Awareness survey that was conducted in 2017 may provide some answers that are useful to Ms Rahayu Mahzam.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When they were asked if they believed that Singapore is a target for terrorist attacks, 59% agreed or strongly agreed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police have also been receiving reports from members of the public on suspicious sightings, and these came through 999 calls as well as the SGSecure app which has a million downloads.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think they tell us that the awareness level is high, but it can be even higher.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for preparedness, it is still a long way to go.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is why we have to press on with the programmes at the community level and also at the workplaces.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the question by the Member on behavioural insights, the answer is yes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our efforts to combat drug abuse are shaped by insights gleaned from in-depth studies of youth perception of drug-related issues.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Minister mentioned about the Youth Perception Survey conducted by the National Council Against Drug Abuse (NCADA).

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And, hence, we have ramped up our social media presence against drugs.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The survey also found that parental influence was key in deterring drug abuse.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Over 92% of secondary school and junior college respondents whom we spoke with, said that their parents played a very important part and they spoke to their parents when they have questions about drugs.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As a result, we have introduced an information handbook for parents and we are constantly reviewing or pursuing research efforts to see how else we can better reach out to our youths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Chairman, this clarification is for the Second Minister.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: In physical harassment, a lot of times it is the family members who report the harassment, and the Police investigate because the harassment will affect the property of the family directly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The borrower will be on the run and he is unable to report the harassment himself.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: For social media, can the family members do the reporting and would the Police therefore investigate based on their reporting?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: At the same time, it will be too much to ask the Police to do the clean up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The family members in the physical harassment case would ask the Town Council to clean up the damage to the common property.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: But in the case of the social media kind of harassment, do the Police have the power to step in and ask the social media business to take down fake identities and fake sites, for example, basically to classify these as cybercrimes to stop the debasement?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A short answer to the Member's question is that as the criminals' tactics evolve so, too, must the Police's repertoire of tools.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What I can share with the Member is that the Police are working on it and it will investigate all valid cases of reports, whether they come from the victims themselves or the families of the victims.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I check specifically if it will be extending the programme where they can have visits when they are not separated by glass panels from their families?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And for the initial incarceration phase, can I just confirm that programmes are offered to inmates during this first to three months when they are incarcerated?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Lastly, I just want to share that public servants I have spoken to are very appreciative of the Parliamentary Secretary's efforts and how hands on he is at the Prisons.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But not all programmes are like that and we work with various family centres to provide the family structured programmes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: SPS focuses on getting the inmates used to prison life.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And so, during that stage of orientation, a different set of programme is being offered to them.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would the Member wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And, of course, Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean.

speaker: The Chairman
text: It is probably appropriate to take a break now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.25 pm.

text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.02 pm until 3.25 pm.
